liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Samson And Delilah** (2 reviews): Samson and Delilah closed the first set, after an opening run of Half-Step into Franklin's into Dancin'; First-set closer Samson rocks so hard that it is the only song the reviewer keeps [11][19]
- **Shakedown Street** (2 reviews): Second set Shakedown Street was called great; the set reportedly faded after Space; Shakedown Street opened the second set at the reviewer's first show, among only two Shakedowns they saw [13][21]
- **Estimated Prophet** (1 review): Reviewer counts it among favorite 1980s versions, for psychedelic screaming from Bobby and Healy's sound effects [13]
- **Mississippi Half-Step Uptown Toodeloo** (1 review): The opening three numbers feature solid, great playing; reviewer prefers this source over others [20]

## Setlist highlights

- **gd86-06-29 01 Crowd Tuning**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [23]
- **gd86-06-29 02 Mississippi Half-Step Uptown Toodeloo**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [23]
- **gd86-06-29 03 Franklin's Tower**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [23]
- **gd86-06-29 04 Dancin' In The Street**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [23]
- **gd86-06-29 05 Brown Eyed Women**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [23]
- **gd86-06-29 06 New Minglewood Blues**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [23]
- **gd86-06-29 07 Just Like Tom Thumb's Blues**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [23]
- **gd86-06-29 08 Stagger Lee**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [23]

## The recordings

- **gd1986-06-29.140313.fob.schoeps.cmc4.mk41.oade.wise.miller.clugston.flac1644** (recommended): source not stated; 22 songs; 131 min [1]. Said about its sound: Noticeable echo but listenable; the Not Fade Away sequence is split across three tracks, seamlessly [22]
- **gd1986-06-29.164035.nak304.thomas.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 20 songs; 131 min [4]
- **gd1986-06-29.144610.FOB.AT-AKG-Blend.Ackerman.Noel.t-flac2496**: audience recording; 20 songs; 129 min [6]
- **gd1986-06-29.nak100.cohen.104996.flac16**: source not stated; 18 songs; 125 min; rated 2.2/5 by 5 [9]. Said about its sound: Amphitheater-style audience sound; the taper sat in the taper section, so the recording is mediocre [19]
- **gd1986-06-29.set2.sennME88.andrewf.96558.flac16**: audience recording; 11 songs; 75 min [10]

## Around the show

- Reviewer, a teenage drummer, was struck by how Bill and Mickey communicated through drumming alone, without vocal cues [12]
- The parking lot was wild, with strange happenings over the two Alpine shows that weekend [17]
- Reviewer felt the second set broke no new ground but kept them moving; says it beat the previous days [11]
- Reviewer says 1986 wasn't a high point, with Jerry heading toward illness, yet this show was still strong [13]
- Reviewer calls this show far better than the previous night at the Valley, though tempos fast and songs short [14]
- Reviewer finds this audience tape more energetic than the soundboard [17]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1986-06-29.140313.fob.schoeps.cmc4.mk41.oade.wise.miller.clugston.flac1644**: taped by Oade Brothers; transferred by Charlie Miller, Jim Wise, Scott Clugston; source: Source Info: (FOB) Schoeps CMC4/MK41 > Oade M118 > Sony PCM-F1; Transfer Info: Master Oade PCM (unknown deck/hardware/software) > hard disk > Adobe Audition… [1]
- **gd1986-06-29.164035.nak304.thomas.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Stephen Thomas; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Stephen Thomas' Master Audience Cassettes; Nakamichi 300 mics + CP4 shotguns > Sony D5M [4]. Also: Oade Schoeps source supplies crowd sound, first notes of Stagger Lee, and a short Drums segment; Other One space is included [4]
- **gd1986-06-29.144610.FOB.AT-AKG-Blend.Ackerman.Noel.t-flac2496**: taped by Ray Ackerman; transferred by Ray Ackerman and Joe Noel; source: Audio-Technica AT8035 + AKG D-12E blend > Sony D5 > Master Audience Cassettes (FOB) [6]. Also: Taped by Ray with AT and AKG microphones blended; edited and mastered in Audacity by Joe Noel; Oade source used for patches [6]
- **gd1986-06-29.nak100.cohen.104996.flac16**: taped by Dave Cohen; transferred by Dave Cohen; source: 2 Nakamichi CM100s/ CP4>Sony WMD6 w/Teac MDX90 cassette masters. No Dolby was used on the Master Cassettes. Sec 2 Row KK Seat 44 Stand head height [9]
- **gd1986-06-29.set2.sennME88.andrewf.96558.flac16**: transferred by Andrew F.; source: OTS AUD: (Set Two only) Sennheiser ME-88 shotguns > patched thru one Sony D5 > Sony TC-D5M > Sony UCX-S 90, with no Dolby. [10]. Also: Right channel pasted over left in four spots, at end of Eyes and start of Drums; Space patched from another source [10]

facts.creator: Grateful Dead
facts.lineage: The Master Cassettes were played back with Azimuth adjustment on a Nakamichi CD1 into a Korg MR1000 at DSF 1 bit 5.6MHz. Subsequent conversion to 24/96 AIFF done via Korg Audiogate software. Redbook CDR standard 16/44.1 files were created using Bias Peak, Izotope Ozone's MBIT+ (for all dithering), and Weiss Saracon SRC (all sample rate conversions)
facts.source: 2 Nakamichi CM100s/ CP4>Sony WMD6 w/Teac MDX90 cassette masters. No Dolby was used on the Master Cassettes. Sec 2 Row KK Seat 44 Stand head height
